After selecting with the predicate weight greater than 0.5, the four edges weighing 0.8, 0.6, 0.9, and 0.7 are selected and drawn in the accent color; the rest stay plain." width="100%"} Calls a user-supplied function once for every edge and selects the edges for which it returns `True`. Any rule over an edge's ID, endpoints, weight, or custom attributes can be expressed this way. An edge selection is the input to the edge-oriented "with selection" methods, such as: - `set_edge_attrs_ws()` and `mutate_edge_attrs_ws()` to tag or update a subset of edges - `get_edge_df_ws()` to inspect them as a table - `delete_edges_ws()` to prune them, e.g., removing weak ties below a weight threshold - `rev_edge_dir_ws()` to flip their direction in a directed graph The matching edges are added to the current selection, unless `set_op=` says otherwise (`"replace"`, `"intersect"`, or `"difference"`). Any node selection is cleared, since the graph holds a selection of nodes or of edges but not both. The predicate runs in Python for every edge, which can be slow on very large graphs. The graph is modified in place and returned for chaining. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [predicate]{.doc-parameter-name} : A callable that receives an `Edge` object and returns a `bool`. The `Edge` exposes `id` (the integer edge ID), `source` and `target` (integer node IDs, not labels), `weight` (a float, or `None` if the edge was created without one), and `attributes` (a dict of custom attributes, or `None` if the edge has none). Edges for which the callable returns `True` are selected. The return value must be an actual `bool`: returning `None` or another non-bool raises `TypeError`, which makes idioms like `e.weight and e.weight > 0.5` unsafe when some edges are unweighted. Write `e.weight is not None and e.weight > 0.5` instead. Any exception raised by the predicate propagates, and the selection is left as it was. [set_op]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["union"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : How the matching edges combine with the current edge selection. `"union"` (default) adds them to it, `"replace"` makes them the selection, `"intersect"` keeps only the selected edges that also match, and `"difference"` removes them from it. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The same graph (modified in place) for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [TypeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the predicate returns something other than a `bool`. [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `set_op=` is not `"union"`, `"replace"`, `"intersect"`, or `"difference"`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The predicate receives each edge's `Edge` object, so filters can key off `weight`, endpoints, or any custom attribute. Here, only the two edges above a weight threshold of `0.5` (`B-C` at `0.8` and `C-D` at `0.6`) are selected: ::: {#2cb602fb .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B", 0.3), ("B", "C", 0.8), ("C", "D", 0.6)]) .select_edges(lambda e: e.weight is not None and e.weight > 0.5) ) graph.count_selected_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: Filtering on `e.attributes` instead selects by relationship type or any other custom edge attribute -- only the single "friend" edge matches: ::: {#fd4f641c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B", {"rel": "friend"}), ("B", "C", {"rel": "colleague"})]) .select_edges(lambda e: (e.attributes or {}).get("rel") == "friend") ) graph.count_selected_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: Because `source` and `target` are node IDs, label-based conditions need a lookup. This selects every edge leaving "A" and then views just those rows of the edge table: ::: {#dedd6e40 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("B", "C")]) ) a_id = graph.get_id_from_label("A") graph.select_edges(lambda e: e.source == a_id) graph.get_edge_df_ws() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
